topic: Logical clocks and the happens-before relation
title: Vector clocks: which update came first?
instructions:
## Three replicas of a wallet service

Three replicas (0, 1 and 2) of a mobile wallet service exchange updates. Wall clocks drift, so each replica keeps a **vector clock**: one counter per replica.

- Before a local event or a send, a replica increments its own entry.
- On receiving a message, it takes the element-wise maximum of its clock and the message's clock, then increments its own entry.
- Clock a **happened before** b when every entry of a is ≤ the entry in b and at least one is smaller. If neither happened before the other, the events are **concurrent**, and the service must reconcile them.

## Do this

Write four functions. None may change the arrays it is given.

- `tick(v, me)`: a copy of v with entry me incremented.
- `merge(a, b)`: the element-wise maximum.
- `receive(local, msg, me)`: merge, then tick.
- `compare(a, b)`: `"before"`, `"after"`, `"equal"` or `"concurrent"`.
hints: `a.map((x, i) => Math.max(x, b[i]))` is the merge.
In compare, track whether every a[i] <= b[i] and whether every a[i] >= b[i]. Both true means equal. Neither means concurrent.

checks.label: tick increments one entry and leaves the input alone
checks.name: tick

checks.label: compare orders events or calls them concurrent
checks.name: compare

realityNote: Amazon's Dynamo and Riak used version vectors, a close relative, to detect conflicting writes to the same key and hand both versions to the application to reconcile.
